content2.content: While responsive UI adapts to screen sizes, adaptive UI adapts to platform conventions. This guide covers techniques for building UIs that feel native to iOS, Android, Web, and Desktop.

content4.content:
Responsive UI: Adjusts to available space (layout changes based on screen size)
Adaptive UI: Adjusts to platform conventions (components match OS design language)
Best apps combine both approaches

Material Widgets: ElevatedButton, Switch (Android)
Cupertino Widgets: CupertinoButton, CupertinoSwitch (iOS)

content18.content:
MaterialPageRoute: Android transitions
CupertinoPageRoute: iOS transitions

content24.content:
Responsiveness: Layout changes based on screen size
Adaptiveness: Components match platform design
Example: User profile screen with different layouts for phone/tablet and platform-specific buttons/switches

content26.content:
Material Theme: Uses ColorScheme and TextTheme
Cupertino Theme: Uses CupertinoThemeData and dynamic system colors
Adaptation: Use Theme.of(context).platform to switch themes

content29.content:
MediaQuery: Access screen size, orientation, and padding (safe area)
LayoutBuilder: Build based on parent widget's constraints
Essential for responsive layouts within adaptive apps

iOS: CupertinoTabBar (Bottom tabs), Modal presentations

Scroll Physics: BouncingScrollPhysics (iOS) vs ClampingScrollPhysics (Android)
Gestures: Swipe-to-go-back (iOS default)
InkWell (Material ripple) vs simple opacity/highlight (iOS)

content41.content:
Icons: Icons.adaptive (auto-swaps based on platform)
Manual swapping: Icons.arrow_back (Android) vs CupertinoIcons.back (iOS)
Assets: 2x, 3x variants for different pixel densities

content42.content:
Icon(Icons.adaptive.share); // Uses appropriate share icon
Icon(Platform.isIOS ? CupertinoIcons.back : Icons.arrow_back);

Mouse Cursors: SystemMouseCursors.click
Keyboard Shortcuts: FocusNodes and Shortcuts widget
Layout: Handle wide screens and window resizing

content47.content:
Dialogs: showDialog (Material) vs showCupertinoDialog (iOS)
Alerts: AlertDialog vs CupertinoAlertDialog

content50.content:
Platform Checks: kIsWeb (from flutter/foundation) vs Platform.isAndroid (dart:io)
Avoid crashes: Don't use dart:io on Web
Conditional Imports: Use if (dart.library.io) or separate files

content53.content:
Conditional Rendering: Avoid rebuilding heavy widgets unnecessarily
Const Constructors: Use const where possible
Platform Checks: Cache platform checks if used frequently in loops

content57.content: Building adaptive UIs shows respect for users and their platforms. By combining platform detection, adaptive widgets, and packages, you can create apps that feel truly native across all devices.
